description: Replaces College Drive pedestrian overpass with accessible at-grade crossing.
Located between Cumberland Avenue and Campus Drive.

chips.text: Approved (7-3)
7 for, 3 against
Administration recommended Option 3, while Councillor Ford advocated for Option 4.
Decision proactively meets future federal accessibility standards expected by 2027.
The current BRT signal system will not be advanced for real-time adaptive traffic flow.
University of Saskatchewan supports removing the overpass for an accessible at-grade crossing.
Councillor Ford argued the overpass is well-used and the safest option for many pedestrians.
The existing overpass has outstanding accessibility issues that a retrofit cannot address.

segments.title: College Drive Link overpass report
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report on the College Drive Link pedestrian overpass, detailing accessibility issues, various options, and recommending an at-grade crossing.

segments.title: Council questions on overpass options
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned administration on U of S funding, federal accessibility standards, crosswalk numbers, signal timing, and the proposed speed limit reduction.

segments.title: Discussion and Councillor Ford's alternative
segments.takeaway: Councillor Ford advocated for Option 4, which retains the existing overpass and adds an at-grade crossing, citing its usage and cost.

segments.title: Vote on at-grade pedestrian crossing
segments.takeaway: Council approved the administration's recommendation for an at-grade pedestrian crossing (Option 3), with three councillors voting against it.

description: Grants tax abatements for 85 affordable housing units.
Allocates $3.4 million for 60 supportive housing units.
Includes a warming and cooling community space.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation operates 25th Street East.

chips.text: Approved
10 for, 0 against
Councillors questioned city's operating funding commitment for warming/cooling space.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation detailed extensive experience addressing homelessness and addictions.
Project targets low-income households and Indigenous people experiencing homelessness.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation committed to serving all community members, not just Indigenous.

speakers.name: Lanny Ahenakew
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City Owned Land - Affordable Housing Incentives
said: Nation faces homelessness, addiction challenges in urban centers.
Suited to deliver housing, support services to Indigenous population.
Combines Western and Indigenous best practices for effective outcomes.

speakers.name: Paul Marjerrison
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City Owned Land - Affordable Housing Incentives
said: Project offers safe warming/cooling space, transition supports.
Provides sober living, long-term support to prevent relapse.
Segregated design ensures safety for all residents and guests.

segments.title: Administration presents affordable housing incentives
segments.takeaway: Administration presented its recommended approach for allocating affordable housing incentives for two city-owned land sites, supporting 85 new affordable housing units.

segments.title: Initial questions on warming/cooling space operations and tax abatements
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned administration on the operating costs for warming/cooling spaces and the process for provincial education property tax abatement.

segments.title: Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation presents supportive housing project
segments.takeaway: Representatives from Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation presented their plan for 60 supportive housing units and a warming/cooling center, detailing services and operational model.

segments.title: Administration clarifies project details and city's role
segments.takeaway: Councillors sought clarification from administration on funding models, monitoring agreements, and the city's role in operating costs for the proposed facilities.

segments.title: Council approves affordable housing incentives
segments.takeaway: City Council unanimously approved the recommendations for affordable housing incentives, including property tax abatements and allocation of UHEI funds.
